svg.title: The concurrency pool every Lambda function shares, and what each control does to it
svg.desc: An account has 1000 concurrent executions per Region by default. Reserved concurrency carves a fixed slice out of that pool for one function and caps that function at the same number. At most 900 can be reserved because Lambda always holds back 100 for functions with no reservation. Provisioned concurrency pre-initialises environments to remove cold starts and is charged whether or not they run. A separate limit caps requests per second at ten times the concurrency quota, which short functions reach first.
svg.text: ONE POOL, PER ACCOUNT, PER REGION — 1,000 BY DEFAULT
reserved · payments
400 · capped here, cannot borrow
reserved · checkout
330 · also capped
unreserved
170 · shared
held back
Everything without a reservation shares the blue slice. AWS keeps the dashed 100 aside permanently, so at most 900 of the 1,000 can ever be reserved.
WHAT THE TWO CONTROLS ACTUALLY DO
Reserved concurrency
Free. Guarantees the function that much — and
forbids it more. It is a floor and a ceiling at once.
Taken out of the shared pool, so raising one
function’s floor lowers everyone else’s ceiling.
no cold-start help whatsoever
Provisioned concurrency
Charged. Keeps environments initialised and
waiting, so requests skip the cold start.
Above its number the function spills into the
shared pool — unless reserved also caps it.
billed whether or not anything runs
THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES WHETHER PROVISIONED IS CHEAPER
Provisioned is not simply the expensive option — per GB-second of work it is cheaper
on-demand $0.0000166667 per GB-s, billed only while running
provisioned $0.0000041667 held + $0.0000097222 running = $0.0000138889 per busy GB-s
The holding charge runs all day. Break-even is 60% utilisation: busier than that and provisioned costs less, quieter and it costs more.
THE CEILING NOBODY PLANS FOR
Requests per second is capped at ten times your concurrency, not by concurrency alone
A 20 ms function at 30,000 req/s needs only 600 concurrency by the arithmetic. But the default 1,000 quota allows
just 10,000 req/s, so it throttles at a third of the load with the pool two-thirds empty.
Set provisioned equal to reserved and every invocation runs on provisioned capacity — but $LATEST is throttled
out entirely, so the unpublished version cannot execute at all.
